domain_e_uiqs_improvement.methodology: UIQS reflects proportion of Domain E items that are non-clone, pedagogically substantive content. Wave 1 (+14.6 pts) eliminated 50 clone items across 10 clone groups. Wave 2 eliminates 45 more clones across 9 groups — similar scale with modestly diminishing returns since later groups target less clone-dense topic clusters. The +1 net-new item (R32) adds quality without replacing any clone, contributing to both coverage breadth and UIQS numerator.
domain_e_uiqs_improvement.note_on_diminishing_returns: Wave 1 targeted highest-density clone clusters. Wave 2 continues into moderate-density groups. Remaining groups are in Sections C-F of Packs C/D where clone density is sparser. Per-group UIQS gain diminishes from ~1.5 to ~0.5 points as remaining groups have fewer clones per topic.

architectural_note.replacement_design: Domain E modernization uses a centralized replacement design: all replacement items (P1-E-Rxx) are authored and certified in Pack E, regardless of which pack the original clones reside in. This avoids modifying Pack C/D Section E items that are in Archived state, keeping those packs' QID counts stable at 500. The tradeoff is that Pack E grows beyond 500 QIDs and the replacement items must carry Section E metadata to remain searchable/filterable by domain.
architectural_note.clone_retention: Original archived clone QIDs remain in Packs C/D with question_state: 'Archived', preserving content for audit trail but excluded from learner delivery pool per CAQS §1.7.1.
architectural_note.implication_for_pack_counts: Pack C and Pack D certified counts will NOT increase from Domain E modernization. The certified count gain accrues entirely to Pack E. This means the Pack C/D 'gap to 500' (150 uncertified each) must be closed through non-Section-E certification work.
